title: Ground-effect image-vortex validation
summary: A from-primitives horseshoe-vortex solver isolates finite-wing ground effect and checks boundary enforcement, asymptotic recovery, analytical scale, and panel refinement.
methods: Finite Biot-Savart segments assembled into one-row horseshoe-vortex lattices.
Reversed image vortices enforce a moving ground plane without a viscous road boundary layer.
Ride-height sweep, Trefftz-plane induced drag, analytical scale check, and span refinement.
limitations: The model is linear, inviscid, steady, incompressible, and zero-thickness.
There are no tyres, body, diffuser, leakage, separation, or moving-road boundary layer.
The published sweep stops at quarter-chord height h/c=0.25 and is not a race-car performance prediction.

commands: cd projects/ground-effect-vlm && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

sources.title: NASA/TM-2015-218804, Description, Usage, and Validation of MVL-15

claims.statement: The reversed image system leaves less than 1e-12 normal velocity on the ground plane.
The h/c=50 image solution recovers free-air lift within 0.1%.
The free-air lift slope is within 12% of the Prandtl finite-wing estimate.
Lift changes less than 1% from 64 to 96 span panels at h/c=1.
The ideal image model produces at least 30% fixed-incidence lift amplification at h/c=0.5.
